subject: business-studies
title: Gearing and Limitations
welcome_lead: Gearing measures debt risk - and ratios always need context.
meta_desc: A-Level Ratio Analysis: gearing ratio and limitations of ratios.
final_note: High gearing magnifies returns and risk; ratios are a starting point, not a verdict.

concepts.def: Long-term debt as a share of total long-term capital.
Operating profit divided by interest payable.
Manipulating accounts at year-end to flatter ratios.

walkthroughs.body_html: Gearing = long-term liabilities / (capital + long-term liabilities) x 100. Utilities and infrastructure firms run at 60 to 80 percent; tech firms often under 10 percent.
High gearing means high interest bills. If profits fall, interest still has to be paid - high-geared firms are first to fail in a recession but can amplify returns in booms.
Ratios use historic data. Inflation, accounting policies and seasonality distort comparisons. Always combine ratios with qualitative analysis and benchmark over several years.

mcqs.q: How is Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) calculated?
options: Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
ROCE is just net profit divided by revenue.

Operating profit divided by capital employed (total equity + non-current liabilities), expressed as a percentage. It measures how efficiently the business uses its long-term financing to generate profit.
ROCE is the wages divided by hours worked.
The level of output where total revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss. It is NOT the level where profit is maximised; profit grows beyond break-even.
Break-even is where the business makes the most profit.
ROCE is the wages divided by hours worked.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.

mcqs.q: What does a liquidity ratio like the current ratio measure?
options: A business's ability to meet short-term obligations — current assets divided by current liabilities. A ratio above 1 means assets cover liabilities; too high may indicate poor use of resources.
A higher liquidity ratio is always better.
Liquidity ratios measure how quickly a business sells products.
ROCE is the wages divided by hours worked.
